gan0: Ganglion Cyst (Wrist Cyst): Causes, Treatment and Exercises | İhsan Eren
gan1: A lump on the wrist: what causes a ganglion cyst, does it go away on its own, and do draining or surgery help? What you can do at home, warning signs and six exercises.
gan3: A ganglion cyst is a soft, fluid-filled lump that usually appears on the wrist or hand, next to a joint or a tendon sheath. It can look worrying, but it is harmless and often goes away on its own. If it does not cause pain or numbness or limit how you use your hand, treatment is usually not needed.

gan14: Back of the wrist: The most common site; usually seen in young adults.
gan15: Front of the wrist: At the base of the thumb, close to the artery where you feel your pulse.
gan16: Base of a finger: On the palm side, a small cyst arising from the tendon sheath.
gan17: End joint of a finger: Near the nail; usually in middle age and older, together with arthritis of the joint.
gan18: The cause is often unknown; sometimes it forms when fluid leaks from a joint after an injury.
gan19: What can I do at home?
gan20: A painkiller such as ibuprofen can reduce pain and swelling; you can ask your doctor or pharmacist before taking it.
gan21: A wrist support or wrap from a pharmacy may help.
gan22: Do not try to burst the cyst; this can cause infection and skin damage.
gan23: Waiting: The most commonly recommended option if there is no pain, numbness or worry.
gan24: Draining with a needle: Recommended if there are symptoms; the cyst often fills up again but may then be painless.
gan25: Surgery: Considered if pain or numbness continues despite draining and hand use is limited.

gan31: Does a ganglion cyst go away on its own?
gan32: Usually, yes. Many cysts disappear without treatment; this can take from a few months to a year. If it is not causing pain, numbness or worry, treatment is usually not recommended.
gan33: Can I burst the cyst by hitting it with a book or pressing on it?
gan34: No. Trying to burst the cyst yourself can cause infection and skin damage.
gan35: Does draining it with a needle work?
gan36: Some cysts go away after draining, but most wrist cysts fill up again; a cyst that comes back may be painless. Cysts on the front of the wrist can lie close to the artery where you feel your pulse, so draining them needs care.
gan37: Can it come back after surgery?
gan38: It can. According to the hand surgeons’ society leaflet, recurrence after surgery is about 10% for cysts on the back of the wrist and about 30% for those on the front. Wrist and hand use can be limited for about 4–6 weeks after surgery, and there are risks such as scarring, pain and loss of movement.
